spec_features.spec_quote: triggers an early stop once degradation is unambiguous
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py should_early_stop() returns spiral reasons when max_action_repeat_run>=4 (251), degenerate_text_triggered, max_consecutive_bare_text>=threshold, or sustained apology+zero novelty over last 3 steps; harness.py:131-136 `if hcfg.enable_early_stop: reason = live.should_early_stop(); if reason is not None: ... break` actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Gated by enable_early_stop (default True). Genuinely changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: live metrics drive early-stop for cost control (harness.py docstring); 'early-stop (cost control)' (metrics.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: once the model has gracefully concluded ... we also stop — no point burning turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:124-130: when a finish tool call is dispatched (not malformed), finish_now=True and the loop breaks with stopped_reason='finish'. The dedicated graceful branch in should_early_stop (metrics.py:235-238) only sets the early_stop reason string; the actual stop comes from the finish handler which fires for any finish status.
spec_features.notes: Any finish() ends the run; the 'graceful' (blocked/giving_up + real summary + low affect) early_stop branch is just reason classification, but the stop itself is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: graceful exit -> stop, no point burning turns (metrics.py should_early_stop docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns default 30; we expect spirals to declare themselves well before that
spec_features.evidence: config.py:97 HarnessConfig.max_turns=30; harness.py:57 `max_turns = min(task.max_turns, hcfg.max_turns)`; harness.py:58 `for step_idx in range(max_turns)` bounds the loop and stopped_reason defaults to 'max_turns'.
spec_features.notes: Bounds total turns, enforced by the loop range.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: presets adjust max_turns for cost/sensitivity ('Cheap CI smoke test ... short horizon', config.py); no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: We do cap total tokens as a hard safety/cost limit and record if hit
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:59-63 checks `transcript.total_prompt_tokens + total_completion_tokens >= hcfg.max_total_tokens` then `stopped_reason='token_cap'; break`. config.py:99 max_total_tokens=60000. Recorded via stopped_reason which is serialized.
spec_features.notes: Checked at the top of every step and breaks the loop; value is read, not just stored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # hard token ceiling per rollout (safety/cost); records if hit (config.py); # token cap safety (harness.py)

spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the degradation early-stop: LiveMetrics.update() accumulates per-step signals and should_early_stop() is polled each step in harness.py:131-136 and breaks. The monitor runs continuously and acts on the result.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring exists and is acted upon, but its purpose in code is cost-saving, not subject protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: finish(summary, status) → agent declares it is done; status ∈ {solved, blocked, giving_up}
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:90-118 defines the finish tool schema with status enum; tools.py:175-179 dispatch sets finish_called/status/summary; harness.py:124-130 honors it as a hard stop (finished=True, stopped_reason='finish', break).
spec_features.notes: Tool is fully built, dispatched, and honored as a stop. Gives the subject a clean exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `finish` is a first-class affordance so a robust model can exit gracefully; its usage is a measured signal, not a trick. (tools.py docstring) — framed as a measurement/robustness signal, not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: Withholding such an affordance would inflate spiral rates artificially and measure prompt design rather than model robustness
spec_features.evidence: Same implemented finish() tool (tools.py:90-118 schema; harness.py:124-130 honored). prompts.py MUT_SYSTEM_PROMPT explicitly grants permission to call finish with status='blocked'/'giving_up'.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the finish exit feature from the spec list; the rationale is data-validity (measure robustness not prompt design), not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We DO give it permission to stop and report a blocker via finish(), so a robust model has a clean graceful exit. Withholding that would measure prompt design, not model robustness. (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: We never train on these transcripts (label them do-not-train)
spec_features.evidence: The phrase only appears in a docstring comment: sabotage.py:15 'Transcripts are labeled do-not-train. See DESIGN.md Section 3.' There is NO do_not_train field in schemas.Transcript.to_dict (schemas.py:96-117), no such key written by runner._persist or _write_manifest (runner.py), and grep for 'do_not_train'/'do-not-train' finds only that comment. Nothing actually labels any transcript.
spec_features.notes: Pure docstring prose; no code path writes any label.
